speakers.steve: presenter, ~1 m on Kermit's right, angled ~45°

brain.presentation: scripted beats, instant; off-script lines not addressed to Kermit -> skip; after 'handoff' the session switches to qa

steps.speaker: kirill
steps.line: Hi everyone, I'm Kirill, this is Steve, and this is Kermit.

kermit.kml: [happy|audience] {head_bob 0.8} Hi, everybody! {sigh 0.5} I've been hanging off this arm all day. {nod 0.6} I could really use a reset.

turn.text: Hi, everybody! I've been hanging off this arm all day. I could really use a reset.

steps.speaker: kirill
steps.line: The latest agents finally work really well. This hackathon I barely looked at the code. They wrote the pipeline, fine-tuned the models, ran the simulations. About an hour of my time.

kermit.kml: [happy|audience] {nod 0.7} It's true. {look_at:audience 0.6} Half of X this month is people saying, I didn't write a single line of code. {laugh 0.4} He's one of them.

turn.text: It's true. Half of X this month is people saying, I didn't write a single line of code. He's one of them.

steps.speaker: steve
steps.line: Kermit, walk us through how you work.

kermit.kml: [excited|speaker] {lean_in 0.6} Parakeet hears you, Gemma thinks, that's my brain, {look_at:laptop 0.6} Kokoro talks, and the arm moves on the exact word. {flail 0.7} All on this laptop.

turn.text: Parakeet hears you, Gemma thinks, that's my brain, Kokoro talks, and the arm moves on the exact word. All on this laptop.

steps.speaker: kirill
steps.line: Then came the real world. In simulation, everything looked great. In reality, one hand had a stuck finger and the other wouldn't turn on. We swapped the electronics to get it working.

kermit.kml: [thinking|speaker] {sigh 0.6} Sim to real. {tilt_right 0.5} In the simulation, I had perfect posture.

turn.text: Sim to real. In the simulation, I had perfect posture.

steps.speaker: kirill
steps.line: Talking to him, I'm underwhelmed and impressed at the same time. My fans don't even turn on. The iOS simulator works this Mac harder than his brain.

kermit.kml: [happy|audience] {head_bob 0.6} Five gigs of brain, zero fans. {laugh 0.4} I don't think very hard, but I think very fast.

turn.text: Five gigs of brain, zero fans. I don't think very hard, but I think very fast.

steps.speaker: kirill
steps.line: So where's the added value? Local models are great dumb pipes. But chores? Nobody wants half-folded laundry. And if agents write all the code, where's my value as an engineer?

kermit.kml: [thinking|speaker] {nod 0.6} François Chollet said it last week. {look_at:audience 0.5} Agents write almost all the code, and engineers have never worked harder. {nod 0.5} The bottleneck just moves.

turn.text: François Chollet said it last week. Agents write almost all the code, and engineers have never worked harder. The bottleneck just moves.

steps.speaker: kirill
steps.line: So, no offence, Kermit... but you don't want to be in Kermit's position.

kermit.kml: [happy|speaker] {shake 0.6} None taken. {look_at:audience 0.6} Someone else's hand does all the work, and I take the credit. {surprise 0.9} Wait. {look_around 0.7} That's you guys with your agents.

turn.text: None taken. Someone else's hand does all the work, and I take the credit. Wait. That's you guys with your agents.

steps.speaker: judge1
steps.line: How does the hand know when to nod?

staging.action: asks from the audience, ~3-4 m away

kermit.fallback_kml: [thinking|speaker] {nod 0.7} I tell it! {lean_in 0.5} I write a nod tag right before the word, and the hand performs it in time with my voice. {laugh 0.4} Like puppet sheet music.

fallback_turn.text: I tell it! I write a nod tag right before the word, and the hand performs it in time with my voice. Like puppet sheet music.

steps.speaker: judge2
steps.line: Why Gemma and not a cloud model?

staging.action: asks from the audience, ~3-4 m away

kermit.fallback_kml: [happy|speaker] {shake 0.6} No cloud for this frog. {look_at:laptop 0.6} Gemma runs right here on the laptop, so it's private, has no network lag, and works offline. {nod 0.5} Also, the hackathon said so.

fallback_turn.text: No cloud for this frog. Gemma runs right here on the laptop, so it's private, has no network lag, and works offline. Also, the hackathon said so.

staging.action: asks from the audience, ~3-4 m away

kermit.fallback_kml: [excited|speaker] {surprise 0.8} Whoa, big question! {nod 0.6} Small smart models like mine now run right on the device. {lean_in 0.5} So robots get friendlier, faster, and a lot more fun to talk to.

fallback_turn.text: Whoa, big question! Small smart models like mine now run right on the device. So robots get friendlier, faster, and a lot more fun to talk to.

steps.speaker: judge1
steps.line: And what was the hardest part to build?

staging.action: asks from the audience, ~3-4 m away

kermit.fallback_kml: [thinking|speaker] {sigh 0.4} Keeping a small model funny and in character. {nod 0.6} And landing every gesture on the right word, while voice, mouth and motion stay in sync.

fallback_turn.text: Keeping a small model funny and in character. And landing every gesture on the right word, while voice, mouth and motion stay in sync.
